How to Write Research Proposal for Masters Dissertation?

A guide for developing a compelling research proposal. Uncertain about where to begin with your research project when applying for a research master's degree? Follow to our advice.

What is a research proposal?

A Research proposal should define and clearly communicate your hypothesis, topic, and anticipated findings. Additionally, it must argue for the importance of your question and the contribution it will make to your field.

Why is it important?

Usually, not more than 2000 words, but verify with your supervisor or research coordinator and the criteria for your degree. Your ability to write in this manner, which is a skill that assessors appreciate in a possible research applicant, will be demonstrated by your ability to present your concept succinctly and clearly.

What should it include?

Project title

Your proposed research should be clearly stated in your title.

Aims and objectives

This serves as a brief overview of your project. Your objectives—the measures you'll take to address each of your research questions—should be divided into two or three clear, attainable, and quantifiable statements that summarise your overall goals. In order to do this, clearly and succinctly outline:

  • How your study fills a knowledge gap or adds to current information
  • the link between your study and the department to which you are applying
  • the relevance of your research questions in terms of academia, culture, politics, and/or society.

Synopsis

A concise explanation of the topic of your study. It highlights the major components of the subject matter you will research as well as the anticipated results. The what, why, and how of your study are briefly covered

Background

A literature review will demonstrate to the examiner that you are aware of the current debate around your study and what has been published.

Show that you are knowledgeable with the major issues, important studies, and experts in your field of study, as well as how they have shaped the contemporary environment.

Expected research contribution

You should take the following into account in this section:

  • Justification for the importance of your dissertation topic or hypothesis.
  • In what ways is the existing research deficient or inadequate?
  • What kind of influence will your study have on the field?
  • Are you going to be extending a body of knowledge, using it in fresh circumstances, resolving a dilemma, putting a theory to the test, or refuting an established one?
  • Demonstrate to your audience that a gap exists in order to establish the significance of your findings.
  • What results will your research contribution deliver?
  • Demonstrate your present level of expertise as well as how pursuing your query or hypothesis will result in fresh insights and information.
  • Describe the originality and innovation of your research.

Proposed methodology

Give a general description of the study methods and Data analysis tools you'll employ. Include information about the tools you'll need, the theoretical foundations you'll be using, and the data collection methods you'll employ. Be sure to explain not just why you picked this strategy but also why it might not have been the best. You must show that you have carefully considered your strategy and why it is the best way to do your study a

Work plan

A work plan is an essential part of your research proposal since it shows if it is possible to finish it by the deadline and helps you achieve your goals for completing your degree.

Resources

Give specifics about the tools you'll need to complete your research work. To determine whether any revisions are necessary and how practical your research project is in terms of financial needs, take into account equipment, fieldwork costs, travel, and a proposed budget.

Bibliography

Give a list of the references you used in the research proposal.  The essential texts you plan to reference and any texts you specifically cited in the proposal itself should be listed in the proposed bibliography.
